prerequisites: A basic level in mathematics, including manipulation of algebraic expressions and elementary functions, solving equations, inequalities, and systems of equations, polynomial factorization, matrix operations, basic notions of linear algebra (subspaces, generators, dimension), calculus with single-variable functions (domain, limits, sign, asymptotes), calculation of derivatives, and elementary integral calculus (immediate, by parts, change of variables). These contents are covered in the prior course Mathematics I.

learning_outcomes.text: Students must have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

syllabus_topics: Higher-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients
Systems of linear differential equations with constant coefficients
Numerical resolution of initial value problems
Practical 2. Interpolation and approximation of functions
Practical 4. Numerical resolution of initial value problems
teaching_methods: Presentation of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Exam of the differential equations block
Tests on Numerical Calculus content during class time using Mathematica
Completion of problems throughout the semester on Numerical Calculus content
Submission of correctly completed practical scripts (within the Numerical Calculus block)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must pass both the differential equations block and the numerical methods block separately. For the Numerical Methods block (40% of the final grade), 75% attendance is required and a minimum of 30% must be obtained on the class tests; otherwise, this 40% must be fully retaken. For the Differential Equations block (60% of the final grade), at least one equation on the exam must be solved correctly; otherwise, this 60% must be fully retaken. Scores obtained from assignments, activities, and tests are carried over across all official calls of the academic year.
